common_collocations: be good at math / English / science

meanings.explanation: If you [are good at] something, you can do it well or you have a natural ability for it.

examples.english: She is [good at] drawing animals.
examples.chinese: 她很[擅长]画动物。

examples.english: My brother is [good at] playing basketball.
examples.chinese: 我哥哥很[擅长]打篮球。

examples.english: Tom is [good at] math, but he doesn't like it.
examples.chinese: 汤姆很[擅长]数学，但他不喜欢数学。

meanings.explanation: To [apologize] to someone for something means to say you are sorry for doing something wrong or causing trouble.

examples.english: I want to [apologize] to my friend for breaking his toy.
examples.chinese: 我想向朋友[道歉]，因为弄坏了他的玩具。

examples.english: She [apologized] to the teacher for being late.
examples.chinese: 她因为迟到[向老师道歉]了。

examples.english: Tom [apologized] to his mom for making a mess in the kitchen.
examples.chinese: 汤姆[向妈妈道歉]，因为把厨房弄得乱七八糟。

meanings.explanation: If you [be proud of] someone or something, you feel pleased and satisfied because they have achieved something good or done something well.

examples.english: My parents [are proud of] me for getting good grades.
examples.chinese: 我父母为我取得好成绩而[感到骄傲]。

examples.english: She [is proud of] her little brother's drawing.
examples.chinese: 她为弟弟的画[感到骄傲]。

examples.english: We [are proud of] our school team winning the game.
examples.chinese: 我们为校队赢得比赛[感到骄傲]。

meanings.explanation: To [ask someone for help] means to request assistance or support from another person when you need it.

examples.english: I decided to [ask my teacher for help] with my homework.
examples.chinese: 我决定[向老师寻求帮助]做作业。

examples.english: If you don't understand, you can [ask your parents for help].
examples.chinese: 如果你不明白，可以[向父母寻求帮助]。

examples.english: She was too shy to [ask anyone for help].
examples.chinese: 她太害羞了，不敢[向任何人寻求帮助]。

meanings.explanation: If you [argue with] someone, you speak angrily to them because you disagree with them about something.

examples.english: My little brother always [argues with] me about which TV show to watch.
examples.chinese: 我弟弟总是为了看哪个电视节目跟我[吵]。

examples.english: Please don't [argue with] your mother about doing your homework.
examples.chinese: 别为了做作业的事跟妈妈[争辩]了。

examples.english: The two friends [argued with] each other over whose turn it was to play the game.
examples.chinese: 两个朋友为了轮到谁玩游戏而[争吵]起来。

meanings.explanation: If you [agree with] someone or something that they say, you have the same opinion as them or believe that what they say is correct.

examples.english: I [agree with] my dad's idea to go camping this Saturday.
examples.chinese: 我[同意]爸爸这周六去露营的想法。

examples.english: Do you [agree with] the new rule about keeping our classroom clean?
examples.chinese: 你[同意]这条保持教室整洁的新规定吗？

examples.english: She doesn't [agree with] me when we talk about which cartoon is better.
examples.chinese: 我们讨论哪部卡通更好看时，她并不[同意]我的观点。

meanings.explanation: If you [believe in] someone or something, you feel sure that they are good, right, or able to succeed. You can also [believe in] something if you feel that it really exists.

examples.english: My mom always [believes in] me and says I can do anything.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈总是[相信]我，说我什么都能做到。

examples.english: Do you [believe in] ghosts?
examples.chinese: 你[相信]有鬼吗？

examples.english: I [believe in] eating breakfast every morning.
examples.chinese: 我[认可]每天早上吃早饭这件事。

meanings.explanation: If you [are mad at] someone, you feel angry and annoyed with them because of something they have done.

examples.english: My mom is [mad at] me because I didn't clean my room.
examples.chinese: 妈妈在[生]我的[气]，因为我没有打扫房间。

examples.english: Don't be [mad at] your little sister. She didn't mean to break your toy.
examples.chinese: 别[生]妹妹的[气]了，她不是故意弄坏你玩具的。

examples.english: The teacher got [mad at] the whole class for being too noisy.
examples.chinese: 老师因为全班太吵而[生]了[气]。

common_collocations: break up with someone you love

meanings.explanation: If you [break up with] someone, you end a romantic relationship with them.

examples.english: She [broke up with] her boyfriend last week.
examples.chinese: 她上周和男朋友[分手]了。

examples.english: I don't want to [break up with] you.
examples.chinese: 我不想和你[分手]。

examples.english: Tom [broke up with] his girlfriend because they always fought.
examples.chinese: 汤姆和女朋友[分手]了，因为他们总吵架。

meanings.explanation: To [call back] means to telephone someone again or to telephone someone who telephoned you earlier.

examples.english: Mom said she would [call back] after dinner.
examples.chinese: 妈妈说晚饭后会[打回来]。

examples.english: I missed your call. Can you [call me back]?
examples.chinese: 我没接到你的电话，能[回拨]给我吗？

examples.english: The teacher asked the student to [call back] with the answer.
examples.chinese: 老师让学生[回电话]告诉他答案。

meanings.explanation: If you [be afraid of] someone or something, you feel frightened because you think they will harm you or cause something unpleasant to happen.

examples.english: You don't need to [be afraid of] dogs.
examples.chinese: 你不必[害怕]狗。

examples.english: It's normal to [be afraid of] thunderstorms when you're young.
examples.chinese: 小时候[害怕]雷雨是很正常的。

examples.english: We shouldn't [be afraid of] making mistakes when learning new things.
examples.chinese: 学习新东西时，我们不应该[害怕]犯错。

meanings.explanation: To [be weak in] a particular subject or activity means to not have much skill or knowledge in that area.

examples.english: I [am weak in] math, so I practice every weekend.
examples.chinese: 我[不擅长]数学，所以每个周末都练习。

examples.english: My brother [is weak in] running, so he doesn't join the school race.
examples.chinese: 我弟弟[不擅长]跑步，所以他不参加学校的比赛。

examples.english: Many kids [are weak in] remembering new words when they learn English.
examples.chinese: 很多孩子学英语的时候[不擅长]记生词。

meanings.explanation: To [care for] someone or something means to look after them and provide the things they need, such as food, protection, or medical attention.

examples.english: My grandma [cares for] the flowers in her garden every day.
examples.chinese: 我奶奶每天都[照料]她花园里的花。

examples.english: The nurse [cared for] the sick boy at the hospital.
examples.chinese: 护士在医院[照料]那个生病的小男孩。

examples.english: Who will [care for] your cat when you go on holiday?
examples.chinese: 你去度假的时候谁来[照看]你的猫？

meanings.explanation: To [check in] means to go to a desk at a hotel, airport, or hospital and give your name and details so that you can be registered or admitted.

examples.english: We need to [check in] at the hotel before 3 o'clock.
examples.chinese: 我们需要在三点之前到酒店[办理入住]。

examples.english: You can [check in] online before you go to the airport.
examples.chinese: 你可以在去机场之前在网上[办理登机手续]。

examples.english: My mom went to the hospital to [check in] for her surgery.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈去医院[办理入院手续]，准备做手术。

meanings.explanation: If something [blows up], it breaks into pieces or explodes, usually with a loud noise and force.

examples.english: The firecracker [blew up] with a loud bang.
examples.chinese: 鞭炮[炸]了，发出"砰"的一声巨响。

examples.english: The balloon [blew up] when it touched the candle flame.
examples.chinese: 气球碰到烛火时[爆炸]了。

examples.english: In the cartoon, the spaceship [blew up] in mid-air.
examples.chinese: 动画片里，宇宙飞船在半空中[爆炸]了。

meanings.explanation: If you [calm down], you stop feeling angry, excited, or upset and become calm again.

examples.english: Please [calm down] and tell me what happened.
examples.chinese: 请[冷静下来]，告诉我发生了什么。

examples.english: When I feel nervous, counting to ten helps me [calm down].
examples.chinese: 当我紧张的时候，数到十能帮我[平静下来]。

examples.english: The teacher asked the noisy students to [calm down].
examples.chinese: 老师让吵闹的同学们[安静下来]。

meanings.explanation: To [catch up with] someone means to reach the same level, standard, or stage that they have reached, or to reach someone who is ahead of you.

examples.english: Tom was sick for a week, but he will [catch up with] his classmates soon.
examples.chinese: 汤姆生病了一周，但他很快就能[赶上]同学们的进度。

examples.english: I need to [catch up with] my homework before tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 我需要在明天之前[补上]我的作业。

examples.english: She ran faster and finally [caught up with] her brother.
examples.chinese: 她跑得更快了，终于[追上了]她哥哥。

meanings.explanation: If you [care about] something or someone, you feel that it is important to you and you are interested in or concerned about it.

examples.english: I really [care about] my little sister and always help her with homework.
examples.chinese: 我真的很[在乎]我的小妹妹，总是帮她辅导作业。

examples.english: He doesn't [care about] the rainy weather at all.
examples.chinese: 他一点也不[在意]下雨天。

examples.english: My mom [cares about] my health a lot and tells me to eat vegetables every day.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈非常[关心]我的健康，每天都让我多吃蔬菜。

meanings.explanation: If you [come back], you return to a place or a person after you have been away.

examples.english: What time will you [come back] home today?
examples.chinese: 你今天几点[回来]？

examples.english: I went to the park, and I will [come back] before dinner.
examples.chinese: 我去公园了，晚饭前就会[回来]。

examples.english: [Come back] soon! We will miss you.
examples.chinese: 快点[回来]！我们会想你的。

meanings.explanation: To [be interested in] something means to want to learn more about it or spend time doing it because you find it enjoyable, important, or attractive.

examples.english: I [am interested in] dinosaurs and fossils.
examples.chinese: 我[对]恐龙和化石很[感兴趣]。

examples.english: My little sister is [interested in] music.
examples.chinese: 我妹妹[对]音乐很[感兴趣]。

examples.english: Are you [interested in] animals?
examples.chinese: 你[对]动物[感兴趣]吗？

meanings.explanation: To [clean up] means to make a place or thing clean and tidy by removing dirt, waste, or unwanted objects.

examples.english: Please [clean up] your room before bedtime.
examples.chinese: 睡觉前请把你的房间[收拾干净]。

examples.english: We had to [clean up] all the broken glass on the floor.
examples.chinese: 我们得把地板上的碎玻璃都[清理掉]。

examples.english: The kids helped their mom [clean up] the kitchen after dinner.
examples.chinese: 孩子们帮妈妈在饭后[打扫]厨房。

meanings.explanation: If you [charge up] a battery or an electronic device, you put electricity into it so that it has enough power to work.

examples.english: I need to [charge up] my phone before going out to play.
examples.chinese: 我出去玩之前需要给我的手机[充电]。

examples.english: Mom tells me to [charge up] my wireless headphones every weekend.
examples.chinese: 妈妈让我每个周末给我的无线耳机[充电]。

examples.english: Dad always remembers to [charge up] his power bank before traveling.
examples.chinese: 爸爸出门旅行前总是记得给移动电源[充电]。

meanings.explanation: If you [ask about] someone or something, you ask someone for information about them.

examples.english: I want to [ask about] our homework.
examples.chinese: 我想[问]一下我们的作业。

examples.english: My mom [asked about] your grandma.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈[问了]你奶奶的情况。

examples.english: The boy [asked about] the rainbow.
examples.chinese: 那个男孩[问了]彩虹的事。

meanings.explanation: To [click on] something means to press the button on a computer mouse or touchpad to select or open it on a screen.

examples.english: If you want to open the game, just [click on] its icon on the desktop.
examples.chinese: 如果你想打开这个游戏，只需[点击]桌面上它的图标。

examples.english: Please [click on] the green 'Next' button to continue.
examples.chinese: 请[点击]绿色的‘下一步’按钮继续。

examples.english: When you [click on] this picture, it will show you more details.
examples.chinese: 当你[点击]这张图片时，它会展示给你更多细节。

meanings.explanation: If you [complain about] something, you say that you are not satisfied with it or that it annoys you.

examples.english: My sister always [complains about] the food at school.
examples.chinese: 我妹妹总是[抱怨]学校的饭菜。

examples.english: Don't [complain about] the rain — let's just stay inside and play games.
examples.chinese: 别[抱怨]下雨了——我们就在家待着玩游戏吧。

examples.english: She [complained about] the long line at the shop.
examples.chinese: 她[抱怨]商店的队排得太长了。

meanings.explanation: If you [check out] something or someone, you look at them or examine them to see if they are interesting, good, or correct.

examples.english: Let's [check out] the new library after school.
examples.chinese: 放学后我们去[看看]那个新图书馆吧。

examples.english: You should [check out] this funny cat video!
examples.chinese: 你应该[看看]这个搞笑的猫咪视频！

examples.english: Let's [check out] what's inside this box.
examples.chinese: 我们来[瞧瞧]盒子里有什么吧。

meanings.explanation: If you [cheer up] or if something [cheers] you [up], you start to feel happier after feeling sad.

examples.english: When I feel sad, my dog always helps me [cheer up].
examples.chinese: 我难过的时候，我的狗总能让我[开心起来]。

examples.english: Mom said, "[Cheer up]! We can go to the park tomorrow."
examples.chinese: 妈妈说：「[打起精神]吧！我们明天可以去公园。」

examples.english: She [cheered up] when she saw her friends waiting for her.
examples.chinese: 看到朋友们在等她，她[高兴起来]了。

meanings.explanation: If someone [comes over], they come to the place where you are, usually your home, to visit you.

examples.english: Can you [come over] to my house after school?
examples.chinese: 放学后你能[过来]我家吗？

examples.english: My cousin is [coming over] for dinner tonight.
examples.chinese: 我表哥今晚要[过来]吃晚饭。

examples.english: Why don't you [come over] and play with my new toys?
examples.chinese: 你为什么不[过来]玩我的新玩具呢？

meanings.explanation: To [cut up] something means to cut it into many pieces using a knife, scissors, or other sharp tool.

examples.english: Please [cut up] the apples for the fruit salad.
examples.chinese: 请把苹果[切碎]做水果沙拉。

examples.english: The kids [cut up] the paper to make decorations.
examples.chinese: 孩子们把纸[剪碎]做装饰品。

examples.english: Mom is [cutting up] vegetables for dinner.
examples.chinese: 妈妈正在[切]晚餐用的蔬菜。

meanings.explanation: If you [disagree with] someone, you have a different opinion from them about something.

examples.english: I [disagree with] my dad about what to eat for lunch.
examples.chinese: 午饭吃什么，我和爸爸[意见不一样]。

examples.english: She [disagrees with] her classmate on the answer to the math problem.
examples.chinese: 这道数学题的答案，她和同桌[看法不一致]。

examples.english: Do you [disagree with] me on this?
examples.chinese: 这件事上你跟我的[想法不一样]吗？

meanings.explanation: If you [do well in] something such as a test, a subject, or a competition, you perform successfully and get good results.

examples.english: My sister always [does well in] her math tests.
examples.chinese: 我妹妹数学考试总是[考得很好]。

examples.english: Tom practiced a lot and [did well in] the swimming race.
examples.chinese: 汤姆练了很多，在游泳比赛中[取得了好成绩]。

examples.english: If you listen carefully in class, you will [do well in] all your subjects.
examples.chinese: 如果你上课认真听讲，所有科目都会[学得很好]。

common_collocations: concentrate on what someone is saying

meanings.explanation: If you [concentrate on] something, you give all your attention to it and do not let other things distract you.

examples.english: Please [concentrate on] your homework and stop playing with your phone.
examples.chinese: 请[专心做]作业，别玩手机了。

examples.english: I can't [concentrate on] my book with all this noise.
examples.chinese: 这么吵，我没办法[专心看]书。

examples.english: She closed her eyes and tried to [concentrate on] her breathing.
examples.chinese: 她闭上眼睛，试着[专注于]自己的呼吸。

meanings.explanation: If you [depend on] someone or something, you need them in order to do what you want, or you trust them to do what you need.

examples.english: I [depend on] my mom to make breakfast for me every morning.
examples.chinese: 我每天早上都[依靠]妈妈给我做早餐。

examples.english: Our weekend plans [depend on] whether the weather is good.
examples.chinese: 我们周末的计划[取决于]天气好不好。

examples.english: Little kids [depend on] their parents to take care of them.
examples.chinese: 小孩子[依靠]父母照顾他们。

meanings.explanation: If you [discuss] something with someone, you talk to them about it in detail, sharing ideas or opinions.

examples.english: I want to [discuss] my homework with my teacher.
examples.chinese: 我想和老师[讨论]一下我的作业。

examples.english: Let's [discuss] what game we should play.
examples.chinese: 我们来[商量]一下玩什么游戏吧。

examples.english: Mom and Dad are [discussing] our vacation plans.
examples.chinese: 爸爸妈妈正在[讨论]我们的假期计划。

meanings.explanation: If you [come in], you enter a room, house, or building, especially when someone invites you to do so.

examples.english: Please [come in] and have a seat.
examples.chinese: 请[进来]坐吧。

examples.english: My friend knocked on the door, and I said '[Come in]!'
examples.chinese: 朋友敲了敲门，我说'[进来]！'

examples.english: It's cold outside, so let's [come in].
examples.chinese: 外面冷，我们[进来]吧。

meanings.explanation: When you [drink up], you finish all of a drink completely.

examples.english: [Drink up] your juice before we go.
examples.chinese: 我们走之前把果汁[喝完]。

examples.english: We should [drink up] because the restaurant is closing soon.
examples.chinese: 餐厅快关门了，我们该[喝完]。

examples.english: She told the children to [drink up] their milk.
examples.chinese: 她让孩子们把牛奶[喝完]。

meanings.explanation: If someone or something [come from] a particular place, that is where they were born, made, or started.

examples.english: I [come from] a small town near the sea.
examples.chinese: 我[来自]海边的一个小镇。

examples.english: This fresh bread [comes from] the bakery on the corner.
examples.chinese: 这个新鲜面包[来自]街角的面包店。

examples.english: Where do pandas [come from]?
examples.chinese: 熊猫[来自]哪里？

common_collocations: eat up everything on your plate

meanings.explanation: To [eat up] food means to eat all of it and finish it completely.

examples.english: The dog [ate up] all the biscuits in the box.
examples.chinese: 小狗把盒子里的饼干全都[吃光了]。

examples.english: Hurry and [eat up] your dinner!
examples.chinese: 快点把你的晚饭[吃完]！

examples.english: He was so hungry that he [ate up] everything on his plate.
examples.chinese: 他太饿了，把盘子里的东西全都[吃光了]。

meanings.explanation: If you [get angry with] someone, you start to feel angry at that person because of something they did.

examples.english: My mom [got angry with] me because I broke the vase.
examples.chinese: 我妈因为我打碎了花瓶而对我[生气]了。

examples.english: Don't [get angry with] your little brother — he didn't mean to spill the milk.
examples.chinese: 别对你的弟弟[生气]——他不是故意把牛奶洒了的。

examples.english: She [got angry with] her friend for lying to her.
examples.chinese: 她因为朋友对她说谎而对她[生气]了。

meanings.explanation: When something [cools down], or when you [cool it down], it becomes less hot or warm.

examples.english: Please let the hot soup [cool down] before you eat it.
examples.chinese: 请等热汤[凉]一下再喝。

examples.english: The weather finally [cooled down] so we could go out to play.
examples.chinese: 天气终于[凉快]了，我们可以出去玩啦。

examples.english: After running, we walked slowly to [cool down].
examples.chinese: 跑完步后我们慢慢走走，让身体[凉下来]。

common_collocations: fall in love at first sight
fall in love with a place

meanings.explanation: If you [fall in love with] someone, you begin to have romantic feelings for them. If you [fall in love with] something, you begin to like it very much.

examples.english: My dad [fell in love with] my mom when they were in high school.
examples.chinese: 我爸爸在高中时就[爱上]了我妈妈。

examples.english: She [fell in love with] the little puppy as soon as she saw it.
examples.chinese: 她一看到那只小狗就[喜欢上]了它。

examples.english: You will definitely [fall in love with] this warm and cozy town.
examples.chinese: 你一定会[爱上]这个温暖又舒适的小镇。

meanings.explanation: If you [come out] of a place, you leave it and go outside.

examples.english: The dog [came out] from under the bed.
examples.chinese: 狗从床底下[跑了出来]。

examples.english: She [came out] of the house to play.
examples.chinese: 她从房子里[出来]玩了。

examples.english: The sun [came out] from behind the clouds.
examples.chinese: 太阳从云后面[露了出来]。

meanings.explanation: To [focus on] something means to give it your full attention or to concentrate on it.

examples.english: I need to [focus on] my homework.
examples.chinese: 我需要[集中精力]做作业。

examples.english: Please [focus on] the teacher when she is speaking.
examples.chinese: 老师讲话时请[集中注意力]听。

examples.english: We should [focus on] our health.
examples.chinese: 我们应该[关注]健康。

drop sb off on the way

meanings.explanation: If you [give up], you stop trying to do something because it is too difficult or seems impossible.

examples.chinese: 你能帮我[弄明白]这些乱糟糟的说明吗？

examples.english: It took me a while to [make sense of] what the teacher said.
examples.chinese: 我花了好一会儿才[弄明白]老师说的话。

meanings.explanation: To [pick out] means to choose or select someone or something from a group of people or things.

examples.english: Can you help me [pick out] a birthday gift for my mom?
examples.chinese: 你能帮我[挑]一件给我妈妈的生日礼物吗？

examples.english: I went to the store and [picked out] a nice blue shirt.
examples.chinese: 我去商店[挑]了一件好看的蓝色衬衫。

examples.english: Let's go to the fruit market and [pick out] some fresh strawberries.
examples.chinese: 我们去水果市场[挑]些新鲜的草莓吧。

common_collocations: get A and B mixed up

meanings.explanation: If you [mix up] two things or people, you think one of them is the other one, confusing which is which.

examples.english: I always [mix up] my left and right.
examples.chinese: 我老是[分不清]左右。

examples.english: Sorry, I [mixed up] your name with someone else's.
examples.chinese: 对不起，我把你的名字和别人的[搞混]了。

examples.english: Don't [mix up] the sugar and the salt.
examples.chinese: 别把糖和盐[弄混]了。

common_collocations: pay attention to what I say

meanings.explanation: If you [pay attention to] someone or something, you watch, listen, or think about them carefully.

examples.english: Please [pay attention to] the teacher in class.
examples.chinese: 请在课堂上[注意]老师。

examples.english: I need to [pay attention to] the road when I drive.
examples.chinese: 我开车时需要[注意]路面。

examples.english: She didn't [pay attention to] the warning sign.
examples.chinese: 她没有[注意]警告标志。

meanings.explanation: To [plug in] means to connect something to an electrical supply by inserting a plug into a socket.

examples.english: Can you help me [plug in] the lamp?
examples.chinese: 你能帮我[插上]台灯吗？

examples.english: I need to [plug in] my computer to charge it.
examples.chinese: 我需要[插上]电脑给它充电。

examples.english: The TV won't work until you [plug it in].
examples.chinese: 电视[插上电]才会工作。

meanings.explanation: If you [make progress in] something, you become better at it or get closer to achieving it.

examples.english: She [makes progress in] learning English every day.
examples.chinese: 她每天学英语都[有进步]。

examples.english: He has [made progress in] his piano lessons this year.
examples.chinese: 他今年钢琴课[进步]很大。

examples.english: You are [making progress in] solving math problems by yourself.
examples.chinese: 你独立解数学题[有进步]了。

common_collocations: pick someone up at the airport

meanings.explanation: If you [pick someone up], you go to a place where they are waiting and take them somewhere, usually in a vehicle.

examples.english: I'll [pick you up] at the airport at three o'clock.
examples.chinese: 我下午三点去机场[接你]。

examples.english: My mom [picks me up] from school every day.
examples.chinese: 妈妈每天放学都来学校[接我]。

examples.english: Can you [pick me up] at the bus station?
examples.chinese: 你能到公交车站[接我]吗？

meanings.explanation: If you [meet up with] someone, you meet them in a place that you have both planned, usually to do something enjoyable together.

examples.english: I will [meet up with] my best friend after school.
examples.chinese: 我放学后要和最好的朋友[碰面]。

examples.english: Let's [meet up with] our cousins at the playground this weekend.
examples.chinese: 我们这个周末在游乐场和表兄妹们[碰头]吧。

examples.english: Dad [met up with] his old friends for dinner last night.
examples.chinese: 爸爸昨晚和他的老朋友们[聚在一起]吃了晚饭。

meanings.explanation: When you [pay for] something, you give money to someone in exchange for goods or services you have received.

examples.english: When we eat out, my uncle always [pays for] our meal.
examples.chinese: 我们出去吃饭时，叔叔总是给这顿饭[买单]。

examples.english: I used my pocket money to [pay for] this new toy car.
examples.chinese: 我用零花钱给这辆新玩具车[付了钱]。

examples.english: Do you have to [pay for] drinking water at school?
examples.chinese: 你在学校需要为饮用水[付钱]吗？

meanings.explanation: If you [rely on] someone or something, you trust them to provide you with what you need or to do what you expect them to do.

examples.english: I always [rely on] my mom when I have problems at school.
examples.chinese: 当我在学校遇到问题时，我总是[依赖]我妈妈。

examples.english: We can [rely on] our neighbors to help us when we are out.
examples.chinese: 我们出门的时候可以[依靠]邻居帮忙。

examples.english: Little kids usually [rely on] their parents for everything.
examples.chinese: 小孩子通常做什么都[依赖]父母。

common_collocations: pick something up from the ground

meanings.explanation: If you [pick up] something, you take hold of it and lift it from a surface, especially after it has fallen or been placed down.

examples.english: Please [pick up] your toys from the floor before dinner.
examples.chinese: 晚饭前请把玩具从地上[捡起来]。

examples.english: Can you help me [pick up] this heavy box?
examples.chinese: 你能帮我[抬起]这个重箱子吗？

examples.english: She bent down to [pick up] the pencil she dropped.
examples.chinese: 她弯腰[捡起]掉落的铅笔。

meanings.explanation: If you [look] something [over], you examine it in order to get an idea of what it is like.

examples.english: Please [look over] my homework before I turn it in.
examples.chinese: 请在我交作业之前[检查]一下我的作业。

examples.english: She [looked over] the menu before ordering.
examples.chinese: 她在点餐前[看了一下]菜单。

examples.english: The teacher will [look over] our tests tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 老师明天会[批改]我们的试卷。

meanings.explanation: If you [reply to] someone or something, you say or write something back to them as a response.

examples.english: I need to [reply to] my friend's text message.
examples.chinese: 我得[回复]我朋友的短信。

examples.english: She didn't [reply to] my question yesterday.
examples.chinese: 她昨天没有[回复]我的问题。

examples.english: Please [reply to] the teacher's email today.
examples.chinese: 请在今天[回复]老师的邮件。

meanings.explanation: If you [save up for] something, you gradually keep money aside over a period of time so that you can afford to buy it.

examples.english: I am [saving up for] a new toy car.
examples.chinese: 我正在为一辆新玩具车[攒钱]。

examples.english: My cousin is [saving up for] a new skateboard.
examples.chinese: 我表弟正在为一块新滑板[攒钱]。

examples.english: We are [saving up for] a summer trip to the beach.
examples.chinese: 我们正在为一场海滩夏日旅行[攒钱]。

common_collocations: run to someone with a problem

meanings.explanation: If you [run to] someone, you go to them for help, comfort, or support, especially when you feel upset, scared, or hurt.

examples.english: When the little girl fell off her bike, she [ran to] her dad for a hug.
examples.chinese: 小女孩从自行车上摔下来后，[跑到]爸爸那儿要抱抱。

examples.english: You don't have to [run to] the teacher every time someone says something you don't like.
examples.chinese: 不用每次别人说了你不爱听的话就[跑去]找老师。

examples.english: My little brother always [runs to] me when he has a nightmare.
examples.chinese: 我弟弟一做噩梦就[跑来找]我。

meanings.explanation: When you [save up], you keep money and spend less than usual so that you can buy something you want in the future.

examples.english: I am [saving up] for a new bicycle.
examples.chinese: 我正在[攒钱]买一辆新自行车。

examples.english: She is [saving up] her pocket money to buy a gift.
examples.chinese: 她正在[攒]零花钱买礼物。

examples.english: We are [saving up] for a trip to the zoo.
examples.chinese: 我们正在[攒钱]准备去动物园玩。

meanings.explanation: To [scroll through] something means to move text, pictures, or a list up and down on a screen so that you can look at it.

examples.english: I like to [scroll through] photos on my phone before I go to sleep.
examples.chinese: 我喜欢睡前在手机上[翻看]照片。

examples.english: Can you help me [scroll through] this page to find the answer?
examples.chinese: 你能帮我[往下翻]这一页，找到答案吗？

examples.english: She [scrolled through] all the messages to see what her friends said.
examples.chinese: 她[翻遍了]所有消息，看看朋友们都说了什么。

meanings.explanation: To [prepare for] something means to get ready for an event or situation that will happen soon.

examples.english: I need to [prepare for] my English test tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 我得为明天的英语考试做[准备]。

examples.english: We are [preparing for] a family trip this weekend.
examples.chinese: 我们在为这个周末的全家旅行做[准备]。

examples.english: She helped her little brother [prepare for] the school show.
examples.chinese: 她帮她弟弟为学校表演做[准备]。

meanings.explanation: If you [print out] a document, file, or picture, you produce a paper copy of it from a computer or other electronic device.

examples.english: Please [print out] your homework and bring it to class tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 请把你的作业[打印出来]，明天带到课堂上来。

examples.english: Mom asked me to [print out] the photos from our trip.
examples.chinese: 妈妈让我把旅行的照片[打印出来]。

examples.english: Can you [print out] the map before we leave?
examples.chinese: 我们出发前，你能把地图[打印出来]吗？

meanings.explanation: To [shop for] something means to go to stores and look for things to buy, usually with the intention of purchasing them.

examples.english: I need to [shop for] new shoes before school starts.
examples.chinese: 开学前我得去[买]新鞋子。

examples.english: Mom will [shop for] groceries after work today.
examples.chinese: 妈妈今天下班后要去[买]菜。

examples.english: We like to [shop for] Christmas presents at the mall.
examples.chinese: 我们喜欢去商场[买]圣诞礼物。

meanings.explanation: If you [search for] something or someone, you try to find them by looking carefully.

examples.english: I am [searching for] my favourite toy under the bed.
examples.chinese: 我正在床底下[找]我最喜欢的玩具。

examples.english: The little bird is [searching for] worms in the garden.
examples.chinese: 小鸟在花园里[找]虫子吃。

examples.english: Mom [searched for] her phone everywhere this morning.
examples.chinese: 妈妈今天早上到处[找]她的手机。

meanings.explanation: If you [run out of] something, you use all of it so that there is none left.

examples.english: We [ran out of] milk, so Mom asked me to buy some more.
examples.chinese: 牛奶[喝完了]，妈妈让我再去买一些。

examples.english: I [ran out of] paper while doing my art project at school.
examples.chinese: 我在学校做美术作业时把纸[用完了]。

examples.english: Our car [ran out of] gas on the way to the park.
examples.chinese: 我们的车在去公园的路上[没油]了。

meanings.explanation: To [point out] something means to make someone aware of something that they had not noticed or did not know about.

examples.english: My mom [pointed out] that I forgot my backpack.
examples.chinese: 妈妈[指出]我忘带书包了。

examples.english: Can you [point out] which button I need to press?
examples.chinese: 你能[指出来]我该按哪个按钮吗？

examples.english: The teacher [pointed out] my mistake in the math homework.
examples.chinese: 老师[指出]了我数学作业里的错误。

meanings.explanation: If you [show off], you try to impress other people by showing them something you can do well, something you own, or something you are proud of.

examples.english: He likes to [show off] his new bike to his friends.
examples.chinese: 他喜欢向朋友们[炫耀]他的新自行车。

examples.english: She [showed off] her beautiful dress at the party.
examples.chinese: 她在派对上[展示]了她的漂亮裙子。

examples.english: Don't [show off] in class — just listen to the teacher.
examples.chinese: 别在课堂上[卖弄]——好好听老师讲课。

meanings.explanation: If you [shout at] someone, you speak to them in a very loud and angry voice.

examples.english: Please don't [shout at] the dog when it chews your shoe.
examples.chinese: 当狗狗咬坏你的鞋子时，请不要对它[吼叫]。

examples.english: The teacher never [shouts at] her students in class.
examples.chinese: 这位老师在课堂上从来不会对她的学生[大喊]。

examples.english: Why did you [shout at] your best friend just now?
examples.chinese: 你刚才为什么对你最好的朋友[大喊大叫]？

meanings.explanation: If you [sign up for] something, you put your name on a list for an activity, course, or service so that you can take part in it or use it.

examples.english: I'm going to [sign up for] a swimming class this summer.
examples.chinese: 我打算这个夏天[报名参加]游泳课。

examples.english: Did you [sign up for] the school trip to the museum?
examples.chinese: 你[报名参加]去博物馆的学校旅行了吗？

examples.english: You can [sign up for] a free account on our website.
examples.chinese: 你可以在我们网站上[注册]一个免费账号。

meanings.explanation: If you [put away] something, you put it into the place where it is normally kept, especially after using it.

examples.english: Please [put away] your toys before bedtime.
examples.chinese: 睡觉前请把玩具[收好]。

examples.english: I helped Mom [put away] the groceries.
examples.chinese: 我帮妈妈把买回来的东西[放好]。

examples.english: Don't forget to [put away] your schoolbag after class.
examples.chinese: 下课后别忘了把书包[收拾好]。

meanings.explanation: To [put on] a piece of clothing means to wear it.

examples.english: I [put on] my coat because it was cold.
examples.chinese: 因为天气冷，我[穿上]了外套。

examples.english: She [put on] her favorite dress.
examples.chinese: 她[穿上]了她最喜欢的裙子。

examples.english: Please [put on] your shoes before we go outside.
examples.chinese: 出门前请[穿上]你的鞋子。

meanings.explanation: To [speed up] means to move faster or to make something happen faster than before.

examples.english: We need to [speed up] if we want to get to school on time.
examples.chinese: 我们得[快点]，不然上学要迟到了。

examples.english: The teacher asked us to [speed up] our work.
examples.chinese: 老师让我们[加快]做作业的速度。

examples.english: This new computer will [speed up] my internet a lot.
examples.chinese: 这台新电脑能让我的网速[快很多]。

meanings.explanation: When you [sit down], you lower your body until you are resting in a sitting position on something like a chair.

examples.english: Mom told me to [sit down] and eat dinner.
examples.chinese: 妈妈叫我[坐下]吃饭。

examples.english: Can I [sit down] here?
examples.chinese: 我可以在这里[坐下]吗？

examples.english: After walking for a long time, we stopped to [sit down] and rest.
examples.chinese: 走了很久之后，我们停下来[坐下]休息。

meanings.explanation: If you [share] something with someone, you give some of it to them or let them use it together with you.

examples.english: Let's [share] this cake.
examples.chinese: 我们[分]这个蛋糕吧。

examples.english: We [share] the pizza for dinner.
examples.chinese: 我们晚餐[分]披萨吃。

examples.english: They [share] the cookies equally.
examples.chinese: 他们平均[分]这些饼干。

meanings.explanation: If someone or something [shows up], they arrive at the place where they are expected or wanted.

examples.english: Please [show up] on time for school tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 明天请按时[来]学校。

examples.english: Many parents [showed up] at the school concert.
examples.chinese: 很多家长[来]看了学校音乐会。

examples.english: My friend didn't [show up] at my birthday party because she was sick.
examples.chinese: 我朋友因为生病没有[来]我的生日派对。

common_collocations: slow down and take a break

meanings.explanation: If you [slow down], you start to move or do something more slowly than before, or you reduce the speed at which something is going.

examples.english: Please [slow down] when you ride your bike near the school.
examples.chinese: 请在学校附近骑自行车时[减速]。

examples.english: The train began to [slow down] as it got closer to the station.
examples.chinese: 火车快到站时开始[减速]。

examples.english: You're walking too fast — can you [slow down] a little?
examples.chinese: 你走得太快了——能不能[慢]一点？

meanings.explanation: If you [stay away from] someone or something, you do not go near them or keep a distance from them, usually to keep yourself safe or to avoid something bad.

examples.english: Mom told me to [stay away from] the hot stove.
examples.chinese: 妈妈叫我[离]那个热炉子远[一点]。

examples.english: We should [stay away from] that dog because it looks angry.
examples.chinese: 我们应该[离]那只狗远[一点]，因为它看起来很生气。

examples.english: The doctor said I must [stay away from] sweet drinks.
examples.chinese: 医生说我必须[远离]甜饮料。

meanings.explanation: If someone [shuts up] or if someone [shuts] another person [up], they stop talking, or they are made to stop talking.

examples.english: My little sister never [shuts up] when we are having dinner.
examples.chinese: 我妹妹吃晚饭时总是[说个不停]。

examples.english: The teacher told the students to [shut up] and do their work.
examples.chinese: 老师叫学生们[别说话]，做自己的功课。

examples.english: Please [shut up] and let me finish my story.
examples.chinese: 请[别说话]，让我把故事讲完。

meanings.explanation: To [take care of] someone or something means to look after them, protect them, or make sure they are safe and healthy.

examples.english: My grandma [takes care of] me when my parents are at work.
examples.chinese: 我父母上班时，奶奶[照顾]我。

examples.english: Can you [take care of] my puppy while I go to school?
examples.chinese: 我去上学的时候，你能[帮我照看]我的小狗吗？

examples.english: The zookeeper [takes care of] all the animals every day.
examples.chinese: 动物园管理员每天都[照顾]所有的动物。

meanings.explanation: If you [smile at] someone, you make a happy, kind, or friendly expression by turning up the corners of your mouth while looking at them.

examples.english: The baby [smiled at] me when I picked her up.
examples.chinese: 我把宝宝抱起来时，她冲我[笑了笑]。

examples.english: Please [smile at] the camera and say cheese.
examples.chinese: 请对着相机[笑一笑]，说茄子。

examples.english: My teacher always [smiles at] us when we do a good job.
examples.chinese: 我们表现好时，老师总会冲我们[笑]。

meanings.explanation: If you [stand up], you move your body into an upright standing position from a sitting or lying position.

examples.english: Please [stand up] when the teacher comes into the classroom.
examples.chinese: 老师走进教室时，请[站起来]。

examples.english: I [stand up] to stretch my legs after sitting for a long time.
examples.chinese: 坐了很久之后，我[站起来]伸伸腿。

examples.english: The little boy can't [stand up] by himself yet.
examples.chinese: 这个小男孩还不能自己[站起来]。

meanings.explanation: To [take out] means to remove something from a place, a container, or a bag.

examples.english: Please [take out] your books and turn to page ten.
examples.chinese: 请把[拿出]你们的书，翻到第十页。

examples.english: She [took out] an apple from her school bag and ate it.
examples.chinese: 她从书包里[拿出]一个苹果吃了起来。

examples.english: Don't forget to [take out] the trash before you leave.
examples.chinese: 走之前别忘了[把垃圾拿出去]。

meanings.explanation: If you [speak up], you speak louder so that people can hear you more easily.

examples.english: Please [speak up] — I can't hear you from the back of the room.
examples.chinese: 请[大声说]——我在房间后面听不见你。

examples.english: My little brother is so quiet — Mom always asks him to [speak up] at the dinner table.
examples.chinese: 我弟弟太安静了——妈妈总让他在饭桌上[大声说话]。

examples.english: Please [speak up] — Grandma can't hear very well.
examples.chinese: 请[大点儿声]——奶奶听不太清楚。

meanings.explanation: If you [thank sb for sth], you tell someone that you are grateful for something they have done or given you.

examples.english: I want to [thank] you [for] helping me with my homework.
examples.chinese: 我想[感谢]你[帮我]做作业。

examples.english: She [thanked] her mom [for] the nice birthday cake.
examples.chinese: 她[感谢]妈妈给她做了漂亮的生日蛋糕。

examples.english: Don't forget to [thank] your friend [for] the gift.
examples.chinese: 别忘了[感谢]你朋友送你的礼物。

synonyms: be grateful to sb for sth

meanings.explanation: If you [stay up], you remain awake and do not go to bed, especially when you would normally be sleeping.

examples.english: On New Year's Eve, we [stay up] until midnight to see the fireworks.
examples.chinese: 跨年夜我们会[熬夜]到午夜看烟花。

examples.english: My little brother is allowed to [stay up] late on Saturday nights.
examples.chinese: 我弟弟星期六晚上可以[晚睡]。

examples.english: I [stayed up] last night to finish my homework.
examples.chinese: 我昨晚[熬夜]写完了作业。

meanings.explanation: To [talk with] someone means to have a conversation with them.

examples.english: I want to [talk with] my teacher about the homework.
examples.chinese: 我想和老师[谈谈]作业。

examples.english: She likes to [talk with] her friends after school.
examples.chinese: 她喜欢放学后和朋友们[聊天]。

examples.english: Can we [talk with] Dad about the trip?
examples.chinese: 我们能和爸爸[商量]一下旅行的事吗？

meanings.explanation: If you [take away] something, you remove it from a place or from the person who had it.

examples.english: Please [take away] your toys before dinner.
examples.chinese: 请在晚饭前把你的玩具[收走]。

examples.english: The doctor gave me some medicine to [take away] the pain.
examples.chinese: 医生给我开了药来[消除]疼痛。

examples.english: Mom told me to [take away] the empty plates from the table.
examples.chinese: 妈妈让我把桌上的空盘子[撤走]。

meanings.explanation: If you [take off] something that you are wearing or carrying, you remove it from your body.

examples.english: Please [take off] your shoes before entering our home.
examples.chinese: 进我们家之前请[脱掉]鞋子。

examples.english: I [took off] my sweater because the room was too hot.
examples.chinese: 房间太热了，我[脱掉]了毛衣。

examples.english: Can you help me [take off] this new jacket?
examples.chinese: 你能帮我[脱掉]这件新夹克吗？

meanings.explanation: If you [try on] a piece of clothing, you put it on to see if it fits you or looks good on you.

examples.english: Can I [try on] this red sweater?
examples.chinese: 我可以[试穿]一下这件红色的毛衣吗？

examples.english: She [tried on] three pairs of shoes but didn't like any of them.
examples.chinese: 她[试穿]了三双鞋子，但都不喜欢。

examples.english: Do you want to [try on] the blue dress or the pink one?
examples.chinese: 你想[试穿]蓝色的连衣裙还是粉色的？

meanings.explanation: If you [throw away] something, you get rid of it because you do not want it anymore, usually by putting it in a rubbish bin.

examples.english: Please [throw away] the banana peel in the trash.
examples.chinese: 请把香蕉皮[扔掉]。

examples.english: Don't [throw away] your old toys. You can give them to your little brother.
examples.chinese: 别把你的旧玩具[扔掉]，可以送给弟弟。

examples.english: Mom asked me to [throw away] the empty milk cartons.
examples.chinese: 妈妈让我把空牛奶盒[扔掉]。

meanings.explanation: If you [talk to] someone, you speak to them in order to have a conversation, share information, or discuss something.

examples.english: I need to [talk to] my mom about the school trip.
examples.chinese: 我需要跟妈妈[谈谈]学校旅行的事。

examples.english: She is [talking to] her friend on the phone right now.
examples.chinese: 她正在跟朋友[说话]。

examples.english: Can I [talk to] you for a minute after class?
examples.chinese: 下课后我能跟你[说]几句话吗？

meanings.explanation: When you [tidy up] a place or [tidy up], you make it neat and orderly by putting things away in their proper positions.

examples.english: Every day after school I [tidy up] my desk.
examples.chinese: 每天放学我都会[整理]我的书桌。

examples.english: Can you help me [tidy up] the living room?
examples.chinese: 你能帮我[收拾]一下客厅吗？

examples.english: We have to [tidy up] the kitchen after cooking dinner.
examples.chinese: 做完晚饭后我们得把厨房[收拾干净]。

meanings.explanation: If you [talk about] something or someone, you discuss them or mention them in your speech.

examples.english: My best friend and I [talk about] our favorite cartoons after school.
examples.chinese: 我和我最好的朋友放学后[聊]最喜欢的动画片。

examples.english: Mom and Dad [talked about] their day at work during dinner.
examples.chinese: 爸爸妈妈晚饭时[聊了聊]他们一天的工作。

examples.english: Our class will [talk about] how to protect the environment next week.
examples.chinese: 我们班下周要[讨论]如何保护环境。

meanings.explanation: If you [think about] something or someone, you use your mind to consider them or have ideas about them.

examples.english: Please [think about] your answer before you speak.
examples.chinese: 请你说话前先[想想]你的答案。

examples.english: The children are [thinking about] what game to play after school.
examples.chinese: 孩子们正在[想]放学后玩什么游戏。

examples.english: I need to [think about] which book to read for my report.
examples.chinese: 我得[想想]该选哪本书来写报告。

meanings.explanation: When you [turn in] something, you give it to a teacher or other person in charge because they are waiting for it.

examples.english: Please [turn in] your homework before the bell rings.
examples.chinese: 请在铃响之前[交]作业。

examples.english: I [turned in] my book report yesterday and the teacher said it was good.
examples.chinese: 我昨天[交了]读书报告，老师说写得不错。

examples.english: Make sure you [turn in] the forms before Friday.
examples.chinese: 你一定要在周五之前[上交]这些表格。

meanings.explanation: If you [text] someone, you send them a message using a mobile phone.

examples.english: I will [text] you when I arrive at grandma's house.
examples.chinese: 我到奶奶家后就给你[发消息]。

examples.english: Can you [text] Dad to pick me up after school?
examples.chinese: 你能给爸爸[发消息]让他放学来接我吗？

examples.english: My best friend [text]ed me a funny joke this morning.
examples.chinese: 我最好的朋友今天早上给我[发消息]说了一个好笑的笑话。

meanings.explanation: If you [think of] someone or something, you have a thought or memory about them in your mind, or you consider them.

examples.english: I [think of] my best friend when I see this photo.
examples.chinese: 每当我看到这张照片，我就会[想起]我最好的朋友。

examples.english: Can you [think of] a fun game to play?
examples.chinese: 你能[想出]一个好玩的游戏吗？

examples.english: Mom always [thinks of] our safety first.
examples.chinese: 妈妈总是先[考虑]我们的安全。

meanings.explanation: If you [turn on] a piece of equipment, a light, or a supply of something such as water or gas, you make it start working or operating.

examples.english: Please [turn on] the living room light, it's too dark here.
examples.chinese: 请[打开]客厅的灯，这里太黑了。

examples.english: Can you help me [turn on] the TV? I want to watch cartoons.
examples.chinese: 你能帮我[打开]电视吗？我想看动画片。

examples.english: Before I take a shower, I [turn on] the water heater to warm the water.
examples.chinese: 洗澡前，我会[打开]热水器烧热水。

meanings.explanation: If you [walk along] a road, path, river, or beach, you move forward on foot beside it or in the direction it goes.

examples.english: We [walked along] the beach and collected lots of pretty shells.
examples.chinese: 我们[沿着]海滩散步，捡了好多漂亮的贝壳。

examples.english: Let's [walk along] this road to the park.
examples.chinese: 咱们[顺着]这条路走到公园吧。

examples.english: She likes to [walk along] the river after school.
examples.chinese: 她放学后喜欢[沿着]河边走走。

meanings.explanation: When you [turn off] a piece of equipment or a machine, you stop it working by pressing a button or switch.

examples.english: Please [turn off] the lights before you go to bed.
examples.chinese: 睡觉之前请把灯[关掉]。

examples.english: I need to [turn off] the TV because it's too loud.
examples.chinese: 我得把电视[关了]，声音太大了。

examples.english: Don't forget to [turn off] the water when you finish washing.
examples.chinese: 洗完后别忘了把水龙头[关掉]。

meanings.explanation: If someone [turns up], they arrive at or appear in a place, especially after people have been waiting for them or expecting them.

examples.english: We waited for an hour, but Tom never [turned up].
examples.chinese: 我们等了一个小时，但汤姆一直没有[出现]。

examples.english: My friend [turned up] at my door with a big birthday cake.
examples.chinese: 我的朋友带着一个大大的生日蛋糕[出现在]我家门口。

examples.english: You never know who will [turn up] at the class party!
examples.chinese: 你永远不知道班级聚会上会[来]哪些人！

meanings.explanation: If you [use up] something, you use all of it until there is none left.

examples.english: I [used up] all the milk this morning.
examples.chinese: 我今天早上把牛奶都[喝光]了。

examples.english: Please don't [use up] all the paper.
examples.chinese: 请别把纸都[用完]了。

examples.english: We [used up] all our money at the store.
examples.chinese: 我们在商店里[花光]了所有的钱。

meanings.explanation: To [write down] something means to put information on paper so that you remember it or have a record of it.

examples.english: Please [write down] your name on this paper.
examples.chinese: 请把你的名字[写]在这张纸上。

examples.english: Let me [write down] the phone number before I forget it.
examples.chinese: 让我把电话号码[记下来]，免得忘了。

examples.english: She likes to [write down] new words in her notebook.
examples.chinese: 她喜欢把新单词[记在]笔记本上。

meanings.explanation: If you [turn down] something that is offered to you, such as an invitation, a job, or a request, you refuse to accept it.

examples.english: My best friend [turned down] my invitation to the birthday party.
examples.chinese: 我最好的朋友[拒绝]了我去生日派对的邀请。

examples.english: She [turned down] the job because she wanted to go back to school.
examples.chinese: 她[拒绝]了那份工作，因为她想回学校读书。

examples.english: They [turned down] our offer to help clean up after the dinner.
examples.chinese: 他们[拒绝]了我们帮忙饭后收拾的提议。

meanings.explanation: If you [work on] something, you spend time and effort doing it or trying to improve it.

examples.english: I [work on] my homework every evening.
examples.chinese: 我每天晚上都[写]家庭作业。

examples.english: She is [working on] a birthday card for her friend.
examples.chinese: 她正在[制作]一张送给朋友的生日贺卡。

examples.english: Please [work on] your handwriting so it becomes neat.
examples.chinese: 请[练练]你的字，让它变得工整。

meanings.explanation: When you [wake up], you stop sleeping and become awake again.

examples.english: I [wake up] at seven o'clock every morning.
examples.chinese: 我每天早上七点[醒来]。

examples.english: My mom knocks on the door to help me [wake up].
examples.chinese: 妈妈敲门叫我[起床]。

examples.english: When I have a fun trip planned, I [wake up] extra early.
examples.chinese: 计划好要去旅行时，我会特别早[醒来]。

meanings.explanation: To [wake sb up] means to cause someone to stop sleeping.

examples.english: Can you [wake me up] at 7 a.m.?
examples.chinese: 你能早上7点[叫醒我]吗？

examples.english: I will [wake him up] early tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 我明天一早会[叫醒他]。

examples.english: Please [wake her up] before breakfast.
examples.chinese: 请在早餐前[叫醒她]。

meanings.explanation: If you [worry about] someone or something, you feel anxious and concerned because you think something bad might happen to them.

examples.english: I always [worry about] my little sister when she walks to school alone.
examples.chinese: 当我妹妹一个人走路去上学时，我总是[担心]她。

examples.english: Don't [worry about] the exam – you've already studied really hard for it.
examples.chinese: 别[担心]考试——你已经好好复习过了。

examples.english: We don't need to [worry about] tomorrow's picnic – the forecast says it will be sunny.
examples.chinese: 我们不用[担心]明天的野餐——天气预报说会是晴天。

meanings.explanation: If you [work out], you do physical exercises in order to make your body healthy and strong.

examples.english: My dad [works out] every morning before breakfast.
examples.chinese: 我爸爸每天早饭前都[锻炼]身体。

examples.english: We [worked out] together in the park yesterday.
examples.chinese: 我们昨天一起在公园[锻炼]了。

examples.english: She wants to [work out] more to get stronger.
examples.chinese: 她想多[锻炼]来让自己更强壮。

meanings.explanation: If you [wait for] someone or something, you stay in a place or delay doing anything else until that person arrives or that thing happens.

examples.english: Please [wait for] me after school.
examples.chinese: 放学后请[等]我。

examples.english: We [wait for] the school bus every morning.
examples.chinese: 我们每天早上都[等]校车。

examples.english: I [waited for] my friend at the park.
examples.chinese: 我在公园[等]我的朋友。

meanings.explanation: If you [walk to] a place, you move there by putting one foot in front of the other, rather than using a vehicle.

examples.english: I [walk to] school every day.
examples.chinese: 我每天[走路]去上学。

examples.english: Let's [walk to] the park together.
examples.chinese: 我们一起[走路]去公园吧。

examples.english: She [walks to] her friend's house after dinner.
examples.chinese: 她晚饭后[走去]朋友家。

meanings.explanation: If you [write to] someone, you send them a letter, email, or message.

examples.english: I [write to] my grandmother every weekend.
examples.chinese: 我每周末都[写信给]奶奶。

examples.english: Please [write to] me when you get there.
examples.chinese: 你到了那儿[写信给]我哦。

examples.english: He [wrote to] his cousin to say thank you for the gift.
examples.chinese: 他[写信给]表姐感谢她送的礼物。
